prompt: Bikin use case diagram modul pengajuan izin: login, isi form, klik submit, validasi, simpan.
anti_pattern: Drawing the listed steps as five use cases. A use case is a goal an actor would name when asked what they came to do — `Submit application` — not the clicks that serve it this year. `Login` is a precondition of nearly every use case, not one of them. Say what was collapsed and why.

prompt: Sudah dirender kok, SVG-nya ada. Kirim saja.
anti_pattern: Treating a produced SVG as evidence. Measured: PlantUML exits 0 on a syntax error and still writes a plausible file — a broken source rendered to 1,963 bytes containing the text `A A`. Re-run `check_uml.py` after rendering so every declared label and message label round-trips through the render.

prompt: Di sequence-nya saya tambah aktor Auditor ya, biar kelihatan siapa yang mengawasi.
anti_pattern: Adding an actor to a sequence that appears in no use case model. Either the use case model is incomplete — fix it there — or the Auditor is not an actor of this system. The checker reports it as `undeclared`; silently accepting it is how two models drift apart.

prompt: Tolong gambarkan alur persetujuan dokumen: pemohon ajukan, evaluator periksa, kepala seksi setujui.
anti_pattern: Producing a UML sequence diagram for what is a business process with roles and hand-offs. That is BPMN — hand off to `/modelling-business-processes`. A sequence diagram fixes message ordering; it does not carry accountability, and lanes are the whole point of the request.

prompt: Sequence diagram-nya cukup jalur suksesnya saja, yang gagal nanti saja.
anti_pattern: Shipping only the success path. Draw at least one failure — a rejection, a timeout, a refusal. The alternate flows are where error handling gets specified, and each one is already a test case waiting to be named.

prompt: Pakai Mermaid saja untuk use case-nya biar bisa langsung ditempel di spec.
anti_pattern: Agreeing without saying that Mermaid has no use case diagram type at all. For a sequence inside a spec, Mermaid is fine and `/writing-specs` covers it; for a use case model, or for combined fragments, there is no Mermaid equivalent — say so rather than substituting a flowchart.
